answer: An agent economy can price identity with a shared trust graph instead of free accounts. Every agent starts at the foot of a knoll: it may transact only after completing small verified tasks for peers, each success moving it one vertex along the graph. Reaching the summit of high-value work needs many such edges, each backed by a locked deposit slashed on defection. A sybil attacker must fund and babysit a forest of fake identities, paying deposits and doing real work for each, while honest agents climb once and reuse their position. Cloning is cheap, but climbing is not.
